mappings.note: Names the Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas as the southern kingdoms of the period - a chronology and geography recall. Not LO-55, because nothing about how they administered or defended themselves is asked.
Assigns writing, sanitation and specialised occupations to the Harappan First Urbanisation - placing features in the right period of Indian history. No LO in this frame covers urban culture.

A state whose ruler is chosen by an assembly must be identified as a gana or sangha - the governing arrangement of a polity. Not LO-56, because only one type is described, with no second state set against it.
Defines the Second Urbanisation as new urban centres of the 1st millennium BCE. Broad historical development, the same treatment as the other definitional items on this phase.
The count of sixteen mahajanapadas from Gandhara to Anga is a fact about the political map of the period, drawn from Buddhist and Jain lists. Not LO-55, since no administration is involved.
Walls and moats read as an emphasis on defence and security - strategies for military control. Not CG-SST2, because the specific administration-and-defence outcome applies.
Sorts the features of a gana or sangha and rejects the monarchy option - the governance of a state type. Not LO-56: the monarchy appears only as a wrong option, not as a considered comparison.
Punch-marked silver coins as a development in trade - economic history. Not LO-55, because coinage is treated here as commerce, not as royal finance.
Brahmin scholars against Kshatriya warriors is the varna order. Filed with the other varna items under the history goal; the equality outcomes belong to the civics goal and to the present day.
Term matching keyed on jati as an occupational community. Social vocabulary, so the goal rather than LO-55.
The Vindhyas as the barrier on the route south is trade-route geography, and the ruler in the stem is only the framing. Not LO-55, because no measure of control is actually described.
Rejects the claim that new cities and states arose independently of iron and agriculture - reasoning about the drivers of a historical change. Technological and economic, so no LO fits.

The wrong pairing is Vajji described as a hereditary monarchy, so the item is decided on a state's form of government. Not CG-SST2, even though the other options are locational, because the key turns on governance.
Statements on the Harappan First Urbanisation, clan-based janapadas and the false claim that varna began under the British. Historical development and chronology.
Names the Dakshinapatha as the southern counterpart of the Uttarapatha. Trade-route history, with no outcome in this frame for commerce.
Defines the moat as a defensive ditch around fortifications - a device of military control. Kept with the other fortification items rather than under the general goal.
Rajagriha as Magadha's capital is a place-and-polity recall. Not LO-55, because the city is asked for as a location rather than as a seat of administration.

The varna-jati order hardening into hierarchy and discrimination is an interpretation of a historical social system. Not C-SST3.1: that competency's equality outcomes sit under the civics goal and concern the Constitution and present-day rights.

Directly contrasts elected heads in ganas with hereditary rajas in monarchies - a comparison of two ways of ruling. LO-55 was used for items describing a single system; this one exists to set the two side by side.
Matches iron metallurgy to its agricultural and military impact against three false pairings. Technological history, so the goal rather than LO-55, even though weapons are mentioned.

Evidence of assemblies of elders choosing a leader has to be resolved to a janapada or gana-sangha - identifying a form of governance. Not CG-SST2, because the administration outcome is the closer fit.
Sorts the real signs of Harappan decline from the anachronistic iron option. A chronology-of-periods item under the history goal.
The Ganga and Indus plains as the setting of the Second Urbanisation - historical geography with an agricultural basis. Not LO-50, which is a climatic-region outcome under the geography goal.
The Shudra varna's expected role in service and crafts. Same social-order lane as the other varna items.

Completes the trio of late Vedic, Buddhist and Jain traditions emerging in this period - the rise of new religious ideas, which LO-58 names. Not CG-SST2, because a specific outcome exists for religious movements.

Trade routes carrying people, ideas and teachings as well as goods is cultural and economic history. Not LO-58: the spread of teachings is mentioned as one cargo among several, and no factor behind a religious movement is analysed.

Attributes a checklist of state resources and infrastructure to Kautilya's Arthashastra - the statecraft and administration outcome. Not CG-SST2, because the content is explicitly about how to hold and provision a kingdom.
Matches Rajagriha, Kaushambi, Takshashila and Shishupalgarh to their associations, keyed on Shishupalgarh not being Harappan. Historical geography and period placement.
Accepts fortified cities and coinage but rejects agricultural and trade decline as their driver - reasoning about what underpinned a historical change. Economic, so no LO applies.
Statements about the four varnas, sub-jatis and earlier occupational flexibility. Social history under the goal, as with the other varna-jati items.
Defines metallurgy as extracting and working metals - the technological vocabulary this chapter needs. Not C-SST1.1, whose rock-and-atmosphere competency belongs to the geography goal.
Places Magadha in present-day Bihar. A locational recall about the political map of the period, not an administrative one.
Guilds of traders and craftspeople read as evidence of organised economic life. Not LO-68, which is about visiting local markets today under the civics-and-economy goal.
Indus basin against Ganga plains as the settings of the two urbanisations - a comparison across periods. The goal's own subject matter.
Defines 'raja' as the ruler, hereditary or selected, of a janapada - the head of a state's administration. Not CG-SST2, because the specific governance outcome is closer.
Iron swords and tools in demand across territories has to be dated to the Second Urbanisation - period identification from technology. Not LO-55, because the artisans, not the army, are the subject.
Rejects the description of mahajanapada capitals as small undefended villages and affirms fortification and political power. Administration and defence, so LO-55.
Ujjayini as Avanti's capital - a place-and-polity recall like the Rajagriha item. Locational, not administrative.
The Brahmin varna's association with knowledge and ritual. Social order under the history goal.

Sets hereditary monarchical rule against assembly decision-making in a gana-sangha - an explicit comparison of two polities' ways of deciding. LO-55 covers single-system descriptions; the comparison items carry LO-56.
